</problem>

<finite_instance>

</finite_instance>

<required_candidate_format>

</required_candidate_format>

Return
- text: your full solution or best partial progress: definitions, the argument, and a clear final answer. If you cannot solve it, state exactly what you proved and what remains.
- claimed_status: "solved" only if you believe the problem (or, when given, the finite instance) is fully solved; "partial" for real progress; "unsolved" otherwise.

A positive answer to the main question is a full derandomization of Erdős's construction to $\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ time; a negative one would be a statement about all polylog-time decidable sets, far out of reach.

**Final answer.** The existence of a strongly explicit $A$ with $1\le\sigma_A(n)\le K(\log n)^C$ is not resolved here and, to my knowledge, is open, as are the weaker versions $\exp((\log n)^{1-\delta})$ and $\exp(o(\log n/\log\log n))$. Established: (i) Theorem A — a deterministic $\mathrm{poly}(b)$ construction of $S_b\subseteq[0,b)$ with $S_b+S_b=[0,2b-2]$, $\max\sigma_{S_b}\ll\log^2b$; (ii) Theorem B — a strongly explicit basis of order 2 with $1\le\sigma_A(n)\le\exp(\varepsilon\log n\log\log\log n/\log\log n)$ for any fixed $\varepsilon>0$, hence $\sigma_A(n)=n^{o(1)}$; (iii) the threshold $\exp(\Theta(\log n/\log\log n))$ is the intrinsic limit of digit-product constructions with polylog-time per-digit searches, so beating it needs a new idea.
